hero.oneLiner: Largest on-demand asset pooling provider in India's supply chain management sector based on the number of pooled Assets, according to the F&S Report, operating a 'share and reuse' pooling model.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Largest on-demand asset pooling provider in India's supply chain management sector based on the number of pooled Assets, according to the F&S Report, operating a 'share and reuse' pooling model.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: LEAP India offers pallets, containers and material handling equipment (MHE) to customers on a 'share and reuse' pooling basis, so customers rent pooled assets rather than buy and manage their own. As of May 31, 2025 the Company had 13.57 million Assets and a pan-India network of 7,747 customer touchpoints and 30 fulfilment centres, serving more than 900 customers as of March 31, 2025 across FMCG, food and beverage, third-party logistics, e-commerce and quick commerce, automotive and industrials. The Company acquired 100% of the equity capital of CHEP India Private Limited on January 8, 2025, which was subsequently merged into the Company.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd. — Corporate Promoter and Selling Shareholder: Singapore company (registration number 202319990K, PAN AAJCV4595K), registered office 12 Marina View, #11-01, Asia Square Tower 2, Singapore 018 961; board comprises Jin Tang Rong and Goh Ping Hao; offering up to ₹ 19,986.23 million in the Offer for Sale.
- Vertical Holdings I Pte. Ltd. — Holding company of the Corporate Promoter: Holds 100% of Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd.
- KKR Asia Pacific Infrastructure Holdings II Pte. Ltd. ("KAPH II") — Ultimate majority owner of the Corporate Promoter chain: Majority (98.8%) owns and controls Vertical Holdings I Pte. Ltd.; affiliated with funds, vehicles and/or entities managed and/or advised by Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. L.P. (KKR).
- Anika Sales and Services Private Limited (formerly known as SKAN Sales and Services Private Limited) ("ASSPL") — Group Company: Identified as the sole Group Company pursuant to Board resolution dated August 26, 2025; there are no outstanding litigation proceedings involving the Group Company that have a material impact on the Company.
- CHEP India Private Limited ("CHEP India") — Acquired entity, since merged into the Company: 100% of equity capital acquired on January 8, 2025. The routed extract is internally inconsistent on the merger effective date: "Our Business" states the CHEP Scheme of Merger effective date is January 2, 2025, while "Risk Factors" and "MD&A" state June 2, 2025. Per the F&S Report, CHEP India was a leading provider of pallet and container pooling services and was recognised as market leader in asset pooling in the container segment in Fiscal 2024.
- KIA EBT Scheme 3 (acting through its trustee, Catalyst Trusteeship Limited) — Selling Shareholder in the Offer for Sale: Offering up to ₹ 13.77 million; board resolution/authorisation dated August 20, 2025 and consent letter dated August 28, 2025.
- TARON Material Handling Equipments Private Limited — Other Indian directorship of the Individual Promoter, Sunu Mathew
- Matyas Possessiones Private Limited — Other Indian directorship of the Individual Promoter, Sunu Mathew
- Frost & Sullivan (India) Private Limited — Commissioned industry research provider: Prepared the F&S Report dated August 2025 exclusively for the Offer, commissioned and paid for by the Company for an agreed fee pursuant to an engagement letter dated April 23, 2025.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Pallets:** Flat carrier structures that support goods in a stable manner while being handled by forklifts, pallet jacks or conveyors, Pallets made from Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) certified spruce-pine-fir (SPF)
- **Containers:** Containers used to store and transport a variety of goods, FLC, Crates, Utility boxes
- **Material handling equipment (MHE):** Hand pallet trucks / Hand Operated Pallet Trucks (HOPTs), Battery operated pallet trucks (BOPTs), Forklifts, including lithium-ion forklifts, Reach trucks, Stackers
- **Technology platforms (in-house):** MyLEAP customer platform (order tracking and management, damaged-asset swapping, reports, help and support), RFID App, Asset Audit App, Transport Management System, Proof of Delivery (POD) App

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company operates a 'share and reuse' (pooling) model under which ownership and management of the Assets sits with the Company and is provided to customers as a service, enabling customers to operate an asset-light model by hiring and de-hiring Assets. According to the F&S Report, the Company operates a full-service model covering warehousing and distribution of returnable packaging Assets. Upstream, pallets are made with 100% SPF sourced from certified, sustainable international suppliers from Europe and Oceanic countries, and FSC certified SPF is used; the top ten suppliers and service providers contributed 60.00% of total purchases in Fiscal 2025. Downstream, as of May 31, 2025 the Company has 13.57 million Assets and maintains a pan-India network of 7,747 customer touchpoints and 30 fulfilment centres, which facilitate storage, maintenance, repair and rapid deployment of Assets; the extensive pan-India network enables the Company to leverage reverse logistics for pallet retrieval at a competitive cost. Maintenance and repairs are handled by the Company's own quality and repairs team, on-site or offsite as applicable, and repair and maintenance programs are run to extend asset lifespan. Technology is in-house and integrated: the in-house developed MyLEAP platform provides customers an interface for order tracking and management, recent order details, swapping damaged Assets, reports and support; SAP S/4HANA and Salesforce Management are integrated to enable electronic data interchange with customers; passive RFID technology is used to monitor containers through the supply chain; and IoT or passive RFID solutions are implemented in forklifts to track forklift movements at customer locations. In-house mobile and web applications include the RFID App, Asset Audit App, Transport Management System and Proof of Delivery (POD) App. The Company consolidated its position by acquiring 100% of the equity capital of CHEP India Private Limited on January 8, 2025, integrating CHEP India's established asset pooling network with its own and increasing its product portfolio, in particular in relation to the container business; TARON is the Company's subsidiary in forklift pooling. Product breadth spans pallets, containers and MHEs, allowing customers to deal with one partner rather than coordinating with multiple suppliers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix shift toward MHE pooling: in Fiscal 2025 Total Income split was Asset Pooling excluding MHE ₹ 3,842.20 million, MHE Pooling ₹ 886.74 million and Others ₹ 121.37 million; MHE pooling scaled from ₹ 75.72 million in Fiscal 2023 to ₹ 675.83 million in Fiscal 2024 to ₹ 886.74 million in Fiscal 2025, making it the fastest-growing line.
- Utilization rate is the core operating lever: Fiscal 2025 pallet utilization 87.46% (87.75% Fiscal 2024, 87.85% Fiscal 2023), container utilization 76.03% (66.17% Fiscal 2024, 39.68% Fiscal 2023) and MHE utilization 81.54% (82.50% Fiscal 2024, N.A. Fiscal 2023). Container utilization improvement is the clearest mix/efficiency gain; pallet utilization has been broadly flat.
- Asset-base scale-up drives revenue: total Assets 13.30 million in Fiscal 2025 versus 7.92 million in Fiscal 2024 and 6.93 million in Fiscal 2023.
- Margin structure: EBITDA margin 56.45% in Fiscal 2025, 56.44% in Fiscal 2024 and 48.92% in Fiscal 2023 — a step-up between Fiscal 2023 and Fiscal 2024 that has since held flat. Cash PAT Margin was 39.44% in Fiscal 2025 versus 40.27% in Fiscal 2024 and 32.17% in Fiscal 2023.
- Depreciation intensity separates accounting from cash returns: the DRHP defines Cash PAT as net profit plus depreciation, amortisation and impairment expenses. In Fiscal 2025 Return on Equity was 4.60% against Cash Return on Equity of 23.45% (Fiscal 2024: 5.79% versus 23.34%; Fiscal 2023: 1.67% versus 15.38%), and Return on Capital Employed (by EBITDA) was 18.01% versus 20.33% in Fiscal 2024.
- Rising leverage funding the asset build: Debt to Equity was 0.87 times in Fiscal 2025 versus 0.72 times in Fiscal 2024 and 0.62 times in Fiscal 2023.
- Contract economics: customer relationships are typically long-term, multi-year recurring contracts with select contracts ranging up to five years, and the DRHP states that the margins earned from these long-term contracts are dependent on pricing, volume and operational efficiencies.
- Comparability break from the CHEP India acquisition: because CHEP India was acquired on January 8, 2025 and merged into the Company, the Restated Consolidated Financial Information for Fiscal 2025 is not comparable to prior years, and the DRHP separately presents Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information for the year ended March 31, 2025 as if the acquisition had been completed on April 1, 2024.
- NOTE: the routed MD&A section is truncated at its Overview paragraph; the drivers above are derived from the select financial and operational metrics table, the Basis for Offer Price section and the first internal risk factor, not from a full MD&A results-of-operations discussion.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Generate repeat customer use and increase business volume from existing customers while renewing the terms of long-term, multi-year customer agreements.
- Capture a larger share of wallet from both existing and new customers by offering a comprehensive suite of supply chain assets spanning pallets, containers and MHE.
- Expand network reach across industries, serve a broader customer base and enlarge the product portfolio — particularly the container business — by combining CHEP India's established asset pooling network with the Company's own.
- Run repair and maintenance programmes and follow quality standards to extend asset lifespan and support environmental responsibility, using FSC-certified SPF material.
- Continue to leverage in-house and integrated technology (MyLEAP, SAP S/4HANA, Salesforce, passive RFID, IoT-enabled forklifts, mobile/web applications) to deliver technology-enabled supply chain solutions and maintain ISO 27001 security standards.
- Deleverage the balance sheet by applying Net Proceeds of the Fresh Issue toward repayment / prepayment, in full or in part, of certain borrowings availed of by the Company, with the balance to general corporate purposes.
- NOTE: the DRHP's dedicated "Our Strategies" sub-section is not present in the routed extract; the above are forward intents stated in the Overview, Basis for Offer Price and Objects of the Offer text.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The DRHP describes network and asset-base expansion rather than manufacturing capacity expansion — no plant, line or capex project with a commissioning timeline is disclosed in the routed extract. Growth is presented along three axes. First, inorganic: the Company acquired 100% of the equity capital of CHEP India Private Limited on January 8, 2025 and subsequently merged it into the Company, adding CHEP India's established pallet and container pooling network (F&S recognised CHEP India as market leader in asset pooling in the container segment in Fiscal 2024), thereby expanding reach across industries, broadening the customer base and enlarging the product portfolio, particularly in containers. Second, organic asset build: total Assets rose to 13.30 million in Fiscal 2025 from 7.92 million in Fiscal 2024 and 6.93 million in Fiscal 2023, reaching 13.57 million as of May 31, 2025, supported by a pan-India footprint of 7,747 customer touchpoints and 30 fulfilment centres. Third, market headroom: per the F&S Report, India had only 15% palletization in CY2024 against 89% in North America, 91% in the EU, 94% in Australia and New Zealand and 50% in China, with North America running a 1,092 million-unit pallet pooling market (55% penetration of total pallet circulation) and the EU 1,500 million pooled units (45% penetration) — India's pallet industry is described as relatively young, having gained momentum and structure over the past 15 years. The Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked for debt repayment and general corporate purposes, not for a named expansion project.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest on-demand asset pooling provider in India's supply chain management sector based on the number of pooled Assets, according to the F&S Report; the DRHP describes the industry as one with high barriers to entry, typically characterised globally as a monopoly or duopoly within individual countries.
- Scale of pooled asset base and distribution reach: 13.57 million Assets, 7,747 customer touchpoints and 30 fulfilment centres as of May 31, 2025.
- Customer base of more than 900 customers as of March 31, 2025, including blue-chip companies; the top 10 customers by Fiscal 2025 revenue contribution have each been with the Company for more than five years, and contracts are typically multi-year recurring agreements with select contracts ranging up to five years.
- Comprehensive suite of supply chain assets (pallets, containers and MHE) enabling a larger share of wallet from existing and new customers; the Company has remained PAT positive since 2020.
- Consolidation of industry position through the January 2025 acquisition of CHEP India, which added an established asset pooling network, broadened the customer base and expanded the product portfolio, particularly in containers.
- Technology stack: in-house MyLEAP customer platform, integrated SAP S/4HANA and Salesforce Management enabling electronic data interchange with customers, passive RFID container tracking, IoT/passive RFID in forklifts, and in-house RFID / Asset Audit / Transport Management / POD applications; operations are ISO 27001 certified.
- Product quality and sustainability positioning: FSC-certified spruce-pine-fir pallets, repair and maintenance programmes and quality standards intended to extend asset lifespan, plus internal quality certifications on deployed pallets.
- Promoter and CEO Sunu Mathew has over 26 years of work experience with prior stints at CHEP India Private Limited and L'Oréal India Private Limited; management team spans technology, asset management, finance, procurement and supply chain operations, backed by Corporate Promoter affiliation with KKR.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer contract renewal and top-customer concentration — Customer relationships are typically long-term contractual agreements, with contracts typically multi-year recurring and select contracts ranging up to five years. The DRHP flags that if customers do not renew their agreements or expand the scope of services, or if relationships with top customers are impaired or terminated, business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows could be adversely impacted. The top 10 customers by Fiscal 2025 revenue contribution have each been with the Company for more than five years, concentrating renewal risk in a small set of accounts.
- Capital intensity and rising leverage of the pooled-asset model — The business requires continuous investment in pooled Assets (13.30 million in Fiscal 2025 from 6.93 million in Fiscal 2023). Debt to Equity rose to 0.87 times in Fiscal 2025 from 0.72 times in Fiscal 2024 and 0.62 times in Fiscal 2023. The Fresh Issue of ₹ 4,000.00 million is directed at repayment/prepayment of certain borrowings and general corporate purposes.
- Depreciation-heavy earnings profile — low accounting returns despite high EBITDA margin — Fiscal 2025 EBITDA margin was 56.45% but Return on Equity was only 4.60% and net profit ₹ 375.58 million, against Cash Return on Equity of 23.45% and Cash PAT of ₹ 1,912.87 million. The gap is the depreciation, amortisation and impairment charge on the pooled asset base, which the DRHP itself adds back in defining Cash PAT. Reported PAT is therefore highly sensitive to asset-life and impairment assumptions.
- Acquisition integration and non-comparable / illustrative financials — CHEP India was acquired on January 8, 2025 and merged into the Company, so Fiscal 2025 restated results are not comparable with prior years. The DRHP explicitly warns that the Pro Forma Consolidated Financial Information is presented for illustrative purposes only and may not accurately reflect future financial condition, cash flows and results of operations. The routed extract is also internally inconsistent on the merger effective date (January 2, 2025 in 'Our Business' versus June 2, 2025 in 'Risk Factors' and 'MD&A').
- Dependence on the pace of palletization adoption in a nascent Indian market — Per the F&S Report, India had only 15% palletization in CY2024 against 89% in North America, 91% in the EU, 94% in Australia and New Zealand and 50% in China, and India's pallet industry has only gained momentum and structure over the past 15 years. Growth is contingent on Indian customers converting from fragmented, manual handling to pooled palletized supply chains — a behavioural shift outside the Company's control.
- Utilization-rate sensitivity — Revenue is a function of how much of the owned pool is deployed at customer locations. Container utilization was 76.03% and MHE utilization 81.54% in Fiscal 2025, leaving idle-asset drag; pallet utilization has been effectively flat at 87.46%, 87.75% and 87.85% across Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023, so incremental revenue must come from asset additions rather than utilization gains on the pallet pool.
- Promoter and shareholder concentration, with the Offer dominated by an Offer for Sale — Promoters hold 391,393,072 equity shares of face value of ₹1 each, constituting 95.28% of the pre-Offer issued, subscribed and paid-up equity share capital on a fully diluted basis. Of the ₹ 24,000.00 million Offer, ₹ 20,000.00 million is an Offer for Sale (₹ 19,986.23 million by the KKR-affiliated Corporate Promoter Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd.) from which the Company receives no proceeds; only ₹ 4,000.00 million is a Fresh Issue.
- Reliance on a commissioned industry report and key-person dependence — The market-leadership and market-size claims throughout the DRHP derive from the F&S Report, which was prepared exclusively for the Offer and commissioned and paid for by the Company for an agreed fee; the DRHP itself carries a dedicated risk factor stating that reliance on such information is subject to inherent risks. Separately, the Individual Promoter Sunu Mathew is simultaneously Chairman, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, and the DRHP's strengths section leans on his over-26-year career in the pallet industry.
